name: Compact MVP Restaurant
_comment: PRD §14 'Restaurant layout'. Compact and highly readable: the owner's travel path must matter, but the space must stay small enough that movement is not a tedious commute. Coordinates are world units on the XZ plane; +Z runs from the street (entry) to the back of house.

staff._comment: PRD §7 'Staffing setup' — the initial worker roster and the posts setup_submit's `staffAssignments` may name. `posts` is the closed vocabulary of assignable positions: the four kitchen stations (each pointing at the station entity above) plus the three front-of-house posts. `dining_room` is spelled exactly as PRD §12's `setup_submit` example spells it, which is why the post id and the zone id differ. Worker roles come from WORKER_ROLES in shared/schemas/game-state.js. STORY-034 rostered `host_1`, revising §7's original 'abstract host behavior' MVP call — reported UX gap: the owner having to personally walk to the host stand for every seating read as the server's job silently missing a body. The owner can still seat a party directly (the pre-existing `seat` interact at the host stand is unchanged) whenever the host is already busy walking another party over — same shared-claim mechanism (`match.floor.seatParty`/`waitingParties`) that already let the owner and server race for the same party before this story. `prep_worker` remains unrostered, per §7 ('Optional for MVP; may be abstracted initially') — nothing in this story's report asked for a fourth kitchen body.

roster.name: Cook
roster.description: Prepares dishes at kitchen stations. Can create a prep backlog.

roster.name: Server
roster.description: Seats, takes orders, delivers food, clears tables. Can be overwhelmed by a large dining room.

roster.name: Host
roster.description: Greets and seats waiting parties at the host stand, freeing the server for the dining room.
